method: Every line of a gitattributes file is a pattern followed by attribute assignments. A bare name sets the attribute to true, -name sets it to false, name=value gives it a string, and !name resets it to unspecified. When several lines match the same path, the later line wins per attribute, so a rule can override one attribute without touching the others. Patterns use the gitignore syntax: * and ? stop at a slash, ** crosses directories, a pattern without a slash matches a basename at any depth, and a pattern with a slash is anchored to the file's directory. Two differences apply here: negative patterns are forbidden and ignored with a warning, and a pattern that matches a directory does not reach the files inside, so dir/** is the way to cover a tree. [attr]name ... defines a macro; applying the macro name sets the macro itself and expands its assignments, and the built-in binary macro is -diff -merge -text unless the file redefines it. The resolver reads only the top-level file, not $GIT_DIR/info/attributes or .gitattributes files in subdirectories, and does not touch a repository. Paths are relative, use /, and a trailing slash keeps the directory path itself; basename patterns drop that slash the way git check-attr does. The page was checked against git check-attr 2.47.3 over random rule sets and paths. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
